i0: **Adverbs of frequency** say **how often** something happens: *always, usually, often, sometimes, rarely, never*.
i1: The key thing is **word order**: they go **before** most verbs (*I **often** cook*) but **after** *be* (*I'm **often** tired*).
af-basic.s: From most to least often: ***always*** (100%) > ***usually*** > ***often*** > ***sometimes*** > ***rarely / hardly ever*** > ***never*** (0%).
af-basic.b1: ***Never*** is already negative, so use a **positive** verb: *I **never** eat meat.* (not *I don't never eat meat*)
af-basic.b2: Use them with the **present simple** for habits: *I **usually** get up at 7.*
af-word-order.t: Word order: I always go, I'm always tired
af-word-order.s: Adverbs of frequency go **before the main verb** (*I often go*) but **after** *be* (*I'm often late*) and **after** the first **auxiliary** (*I have never been, I can't always come*).
af-word-order.b0.2.1: *I **have never** seen it. You **can always** call me.*
af-word-order.b0.3.1: ***Do** you **often** go out? **Are** you **always** this busy?*
af-word-order.b0.4.1: *I **don't usually** eat meat. She **isn't often** late.*
af-word-order.b1: ***Sometimes, usually*** and ***often*** can also go at the **start** or **end**: ***Sometimes** I walk to work. I walk to work **sometimes**.*
af-word-order.b2: ***Always*** and ***never*** don't usually go at the start (except *Never…* for emphasis in formal English).
af-how-often.t: How often? Once a week, every day, twice a month
af-how-often.s: Ask ***How often…?*** and answer with **expressions of frequency**: *every day, once a week, twice a month, three times a year, every other day*. These usually go at the **end** of the sentence.
af-how-often.b0.1.1: *We eat out **once a week**. She calls **twice a day**.*
af-how-often.b0.2.1: *I wash my hair **every other day**.* (= every second day)
af-how-often.b0.4.0: *from time to time / now and then*
af-how-often.b1: Say ***once*** (1) and ***twice*** (2), then ***three times, four times***…: *I've been there **twice**.* (*two times* is common in speech, but *twice* is better)
